package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects all versions using compromised shared JS libraries)
package_info.why_malicious: The injected JavaScript skimming script is designed to steal credit card information from users of over 200 online university campus stores by intercepting payment data and exfiltrating it to attacker-controlled infrastructure. This is a classic example of Magecart-style web skimming malware.

execution_context.file_location: Shared JavaScript library loaded by PrismWeb commerce platform (e.g., /js/shared.js)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the payment form submission event, collects credit card data from input fields, and exfiltrates this data to an attacker-controlled domain via an HTTP request, resulting in theft of payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting sensitive payment data in the browser and sending it to an external domain is a hallmark of web skimming attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce scripts should never exfiltrate payment data to third-party domains; payment data should only be sent to trusted payment processors.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form validation scripts may read payment fields, but should not transmit data externally.
key_indicators: Event listener on payment form submission
Network request to untrusted external domain

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises PrismWeb shared JavaScript library and injects skimming code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded by all online stores using the shared library.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript executes in the browser when a user visits a compromised store and fills out the payment form.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credit card data is intercepted at the point of form submission.

attack_chain.action: Stolen payment data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker collects and monetizes stolen credit card information.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript event listeners on payment forms that send data to external domains
Unexpected network requests containing payment data at form submission
Obfuscated or injected scripts in shared JavaScript libraries
file_indicators: Modifications to shared JavaScript files (e.g., /js/shared.js) not present in official releases
Presence of new or obfuscated code blocks in e-commerce platform scripts
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with the legitimate payment processor
Unusual traffic to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., attacker.com/collect)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for changes in shared JavaScript libraries, especially those loaded by payment pages. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict data exfiltration. Analyze network traffic from payment pages for unexpected destinations. Scan for event listeners on payment forms that transmit data externally. Employ file integrity monitoring on e-commerce platform scripts.
